title: Desk Q&A — The Allowance Ceiling at Settlement of an Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscription
content:
# The Allowance Ceiling at Settlement

Questions answered on the ceiling that holds the settlement allowance on a subscription under Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscriptions. The long standing count is 18 whole months and the established count is 6 whole months; the long standing ceiling is USD 250, the established ceiling USD 150 and the opening ceiling USD 60.

## Rule

Where the subscription's current term has run the long standing count of whole months or more and the subscription stands active, the allowance ceiling is the long standing ceiling. Where the subscription's current term has run the established count of whole months or more but fewer than the long standing count and the subscription stands active, the allowance ceiling is the established ceiling. In every other case the allowance ceiling is the opening ceiling.

## Questions

**How is the age of the term measured?** In whole months from the term start date standing on the subscription record to the day of settlement.

**A term that has run 18 whole months on an active subscription.** The long standing ceiling, USD 250. At 24 whole months, the same.

**A term that has run 6 whole months on an active subscription.** The established ceiling, USD 150. At 17 whole months, still USD 150.

**A term that has run 5 whole months on an active subscription.** The opening ceiling, USD 60.

**A term that has run 30 whole months but the subscription stands suspended, or in its renewal window.** Neither of the first two limbs is met, because both require the subscription to stand active; the opening ceiling of USD 60 applies.

## Summary

| Whole months the current term has run | Status | Ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| 18 or more | active | USD 250 |
| 6 to 17 | active | USD 150 |
| 5 or fewer | active | USD 60 |
| any | any other status | USD 60 |
